findings.title: No re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.description:
The cache is read under `RLock` (lines 41-43), the lock is released, and then the exclusive lock is taken (line 48) with no second look at `entryPointAssetsCache`. In non-dev mode, every goroutine that saw `nil` during a cold start queues on `Lock()` and then re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` in turn, even though the first one already filled the cache. Each one also replaces the cached pointer with a new, equivalent object.

The fix is the standard double-checked pattern: after `Lock()`, add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Alternatively, use `singleflight` or `sync.Once`-style initialisation for the non-dev path.

findings.title: Failed loads are now serialized behind an exclusive lock on every request
findings.description:
When the load fails (manifest missing or malformed), line 69 stores `nil` in the cache, so the fast path never hits. Every later call takes the exclusive lock and repeats the file I/O and JSON decode while holding it.

Before this change those retries ran concurrently; now they run one at a time. The affected callers are the index page (`pkg/api/index.go:82`), the frontend settings hash (`pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62`) and the panic recovery handler (`pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141`), so a broken manifest turns into a global contention point on those paths.

The same applies to every request in `setting.Dev`, where the cache is bypassed by design. There the `RLock` round trip is also wasted work.

Consider doing the I/O outside the lock and locking only for the pointer swap, and not overwriting a previously good cache entry with `nil` on error.

findings.title: No test covers `GetWebAssets` or the concurrency fix
findings.description:
The change exists to fix a data race, but `webassets_test.go` only exercises `readWebAssetsFromFile` and a skipped CDN test. `GetWebAssets` has no test at all, so nothing run under `go test -race` would catch a regression of the locking.

A small test would cover it: spawn N goroutines calling `GetWebAssets` against a `setting.Cfg` whose `StaticRootPath` points at a testdata manifest, in both dev and non-dev `Env`. That test would also pin down the cache-hit behaviour.

findings.title: Network I/O would be held under the write lock if the CDN path is enabled
findings.description: `cdn` is hardcoded to `""`, so `readWebAssetsFromCDN` is currently unreachable from `GetWebAssets`. If it is enabled later, the call would run inside the exclusive lock using `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout, bounded only by the request context of whichever caller got there first. Other callers block on a mutex that does not honour their own context. No action is needed now, but restructure the lock scope before turning that branch on.

findings.title: Cached pointer is shared and mutable; safe today only because callers are read-only
findings.description: The mutex protects the pointer variable, not the `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` it points to. All three callers only read the result, and `SetContentDeliveryURL` (`pkg/api/dtos/index.go:51`), which mutates in place, is only called on the fresh object before it is published at line 69. So there is no race at present. A future caller that mutates the returned value, for example by calling `SetContentDeliveryURL` on it, would reintroduce a race the mutex cannot prevent. A doc comment on `GetWebAssets` saying the result must be treated as immutable would make that contract explicit.

findings.title: Cache ignores its inputs (pre-existing, acknowledged by TODO)
findings.description: The package-level cache is keyed on nothing, so the first `cfg`/`license` pair to fill it wins for the life of the process. This matters for tests or multi-instance setups in one binary. The new `TODO: get rid of global state` comment acknowledges it; it is not introduced by this diff.

findings.title: Lock usage is correct and race-free for the guarded variable
findings.description: All accesses to `entryPointAssetsCache` (lines 42, 69, 70) happen under the appropriate lock. `RUnlock` is called before `Lock`, so there is no self-deadlock from attempting a lock upgrade. The `defer Unlock()` releases the mutex during panic unwinding before the recovery middleware re-enters `GetWebAssets` at `pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141`, so that path cannot deadlock. The mutex naming and placement next to the variable it guards follow normal Go convention.
